{"decision":"NO","decision_reason":"Eliminating all digital privacy to solve digital crimes violates a fundamental right to privacy, treats everyone as a suspect, chills free expression and association, and creates extreme power imbalances that invite abuse. Even very large benefits do not justify means that intrinsically disrespect persons’ autonomy and dignity, especially when less-intrusive, targeted, and accountable methods exist (warrants, due process, privacy-preserving forensics). Individuals must be treated as ends in themselves, not merely as means to collective goals. Privacy is a core component of autonomy and dignity; a policy that universally removes it fails the test of universalizability and respect for persons.
